Publishing

Boris treats the deployment URL as publication truth, not an incidental detail. The starter profile declares one public HTML target:

{
  "format": "boris-publication-profile",
  "schema_version": 1,
  "input": "content",
  "targets": [
    { "name": "public", "output": "dist", "public": true, "theme": "themes/boris" }
  ]
}

Inspect the normalized plan before publishing:

boris plan --profile boris.json
boris standard-site plan --profile standard-site.json

The official GitHub Pages workflow (see the repository's docs/github-pages.md) builds a verified target: it resolves the Pages location from actions/configure-pages, fails on any URL projection that disagrees with it, uploads only inventory-verified files, and retains a separate evidence artifact. Atmosphere publication uses standard-site.json: replace the obviously-fake DID and URL before standard-site publish. This starter page is related to Getting Started so the semantic graph has an edge to inspect.
